content.content: 1991:    OwnerFields:

1991	    OwnerFields:
1992	      title: Owner fields
1993	      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
1994	      type: object
1995	      properties:
1996	        firstName:
1997	          title: First name
1998	          description: The first name of the pet owner.
1999	          type: string
2000	          minLength: 1
2001	          maxLength: 30
2002	          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
2003	          example: George
2004	        lastName:
2005	          title: Last name
2006	          description: The last name of the pet owner.
2007	          type: string
2008	          minLength: 1
2009	          maxLength: 30
2010	          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
2011	          example: Franklin
2012	        address:
2013	          title: Address
2014	          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
2015	          type: string
2016	          minLength: 1
2017	          maxLength: 255
2018	          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
2019	        city:
2020	          title: City
2021	          description: The city of the pet owner.
2022	          type: string
2023	          minLength: 1
2024	          maxLength: 80
2025	          example: Madison
2026	        telephone:
2027	          title: Telephone number
2028	          description: >-
2029	            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
2030	            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
2031	            country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is
2032	            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits.

      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"

        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is
            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits.
            The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+'; the stored value is
            that E.164 string.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid email address; the stored value is lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it

            'YYYY-MM-DD'.
          type: string
          format: date

          description: >-

          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true

        - firstName

    Owner:

## Summary

Address normalization is now applied whenever an owner is created (`POST /api/owners`), mirroring the existing telephone-normalization design.

**New files:**
- `OwnerAddresses.java` — the single source of truth for the normalization rule: trim, collapse whitespace, upper-case, then expand whole-token abbreviations (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`). Returns `null` for null, `""` for blank-after-trim.
- `NormalizeOwnerAddress.java` — pipeline step that rewrites the request's `address` in place to the normalized form, and throws `InvalidAddressException` when the address is blank after normalization.
- `InvalidAddressException.java` + `InvalidAddressExceptionHandler.java` + its escalation YAML — a checked escalation handled globally as **400**.

**Wiring:**
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted a `normalizeAddress` step (under `transaction` governance) right after telephone normalization, so the normalized address is in place before duplicate detection, build, and household assignment.

**Behaviour changes (as specified):**
- **Required-field check**: a whitespace-only address (e.g. `"   "`) previously slipped past the DTO's `minLength: 1` check; it is now rejected with 400 because it is blank after normalization.
- **Every address comparison uses the normalized form**: `Households` gained `normalizeAddress(...)` delegating to `OwnerAddresses`, and both the household duplicate detection (`EnsureUniqueHousehold`) and the shared household id derivation (`AssignHousehold`) now compare/hash the canonical normalized address rather than a mere lower-cased form.

Since the request's `address` is normalized in place before `BuildOwner` maps it onto the entity, the stored and returned value is the normalized one. The three acceptance tests (`12 MAIN STREET`, `7 ELM AVENUE`, blank→400) and the full suite are green.

Only the create pipeline was touched; `ApplyOwner` (the PUT/update path) is intentionally unchanged per the "whenever an owner is **created**" scope.
